1.1.evidence:
I. GENERAL
Women and children have an important role in the development of a nation. Women as mothers of the nation who will give birth to children and children as the next generation of the nation are the capital of national development that need to obtain legal protection from acts of gender-based violence and violence against children.
Gender-based violence and violence against children nowadays are increasingly rising in number. Several forms of acts of violence against women and children that occur in society can be in the form of social harassment, rape, trafficking of women and children, pornography, sexual exploitation, neglect, domestic violence. Therefore, legal instruments are needed that can guarantee the implementation of protection of the rights of women and children both at the national and regional levels.
In order to realize the protection of the rights of women and children from the threat of acts of violence as referred to above, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Protection for Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Violence Against Children.
1.1.rationale: The policy text explicitly lists “domestic violence” as one of the forms of violence against women and children addressed by the regulation.

1.2.evidence:
CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Central Government hereinafter referred to as Government is the President of the Republic of Indonesia who holds the governmental power of the State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.
2. Region is Kudus Regency.
3. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of regional government administration.
4. Regent is the Regent of Kudus.
5. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter referred to as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Kudus Regency.
6. Regional Apparatus Work Unit hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD is the Regional Apparatus Work Unit that oversees women's empowerment and child protection.
7. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
8. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
9. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of victims carried out by family, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
10. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
11. Implementation of protection is a series of activities aimed at preventing the occurrence of violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation carried out by the relevant SKPD.
12. Violence is any form of unlawful act that can result in or cause danger to a person whether physical, sexual, psychological or economic in nature.
13. Gender-Based Violence is any form of restriction, exclusion, differentiation and all forms of treatment carried out on the basis of gender and aimed at reducing, eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or use of human rights, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological and economic violence.
14. Violence Against Children is any form of restriction, differentiation, exclusion and all forms of treatment carried out against children, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological, and economic violence.
15. Physical Violence is any act that results in pain, illness, or serious injury.
16. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural and/or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
17. Psychological Violence or psychic violence is any act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering in a person.
18. Economic Violence is any act that may include restricting a person's right to work decently inside or outside the home and also acts of neglecting family members in the form of not providing a decent living, care or maintenance.
19. Victim of Gender-Based Violence is a person who due to their gender experiences physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual suffering, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
20. Child Victim of Violence is a child who receives harsh treatment whether physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
21. Victim Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to be more empowered, whether physically, psychologically, socially, economically or sexually.
22. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the purpose of self-empowerment of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children to resolve the problems they face.
23. Integrated Services is a series of activities to provide protection for victims of gender-based violence and children carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as a unified implementation, prevention efforts, health services, medicolegal services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children.
24. Social Reintegration is the process of preparing the community and victims that supports the reunification of victims into the family environment, family substitutes that can provide protection and fulfillment of victims' needs.
25. Safe House (shelter) is a temporary residence used to provide protection to victims in accordance with determined operational standards.
26. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations, and/or community organizations.
1.2.rationale: The policy explicitly defines “Sexual Violence,” indicating that sexual violence is included within the scope of violence addressed.

2.1.evidence:
CHAPTER VII
COOPERATION
Article 17
(1) In providing protection for victims of gender-based violence and children, the Regional Government cooperates with the Government, Provincial Government, and Regency/City Government, and other institutions.
(2) Cooperation between the Regional Government and the Government and Provincial Government as referred to in paragraph (1) includes consultation, coordination and reporting.
(3) Cooperation between the Regional Government and Regency/City as referred to in paragraph (1) includes coordination, advocacy, referral, repatriation, social reintegration, facilitation of integrated service system development, monitoring, evaluation and reporting.
2.1.rationale: The policy describes formal cooperation by the Regional Government with the Government, Provincial Government, and Regency/City Government, including consultation, coordination, reporting, and other cross-jurisdictional activities—indicating an institutional network across jurisdictions.

2.2.rationale: The policy establishes an Integrated Service whose membership explicitly includes non-governmental institutions, and assigns it coordination/cooperation duties, constituting a mechanism for collaboration with non-government service providers.

2.3.evidence:
Article 14
Monitoring and reporting as referred to in Article 7 paragraph (3) letter f shall be conducted on all aspects of integrated service activities in the form of supervision, documentation and evaluation of cases of gender-based and child violence.
2.3.rationale: The policy mandates monitoring and reporting of integrated service activities including supervision, documentation, and evaluation of cases, which constitutes a case documentation/information component relevant to data collection.

2.4.rationale: While the policy references principles such as gender justice and equality, none of the provided passages mention gender mainstreaming institutionalisation or a dedicated gender mainstreaming working group/mechanism to deliver VAW policies and programs.

2.5.rationale: The policy gives the Regional Government authority to “increase the capacity of service provider institutions,” which implies capacity-building measures for institutions involved in service delivery, even though specific training modalities are not detailed.

2.6.evidence:

2.6.rationale: The policy explicitly provides for monitoring and reporting across integrated service activities, including supervision, documentation, and evaluation of cases, which directly addresses monitoring and evaluation of implementation/service delivery.

3.1.rationale: The policy explicitly provides for the establishment of an Integrated Service, including its composition and duties, indicating an integrated service unit for addressing gender-based violence (including VAW).

3.2.rationale: While the text references police as part of broader protection and coordination, none of the provided passages explicitly establish or require a specialised service unit for VAW victims within police offices.

3.3.rationale: The passages mention monitoring/reporting and community conveying information to authorities, but they do not establish a dedicated service unit (e.g., hotline/complaints desk) specifically to receive reports or complaints of violence.

3.4.rationale: The policy explicitly includes provision of safe houses (shelters) as a government obligation, indicating a service for safety/protection shelter.

3.5.rationale: The policy specifies legal protection measures including assistance during the legal process, demonstrating provision of legal assistance services for victims.

3.6.rationale: The policy explicitly includes physical recovery at health service institutions and medicolegal services as part of recovery efforts, indicating provision of health/medical services.

3.7.rationale: The policy explicitly includes psychosocial recovery and assistance within recovery and social reintegration efforts, indicating psychosocial counseling/support services.

3.8.rationale: The policy explicitly includes spiritual guidance services as part of recovery and social reintegration efforts, indicating religious/spiritual counseling support.

3.9.rationale: The Integrated Service is assigned duties including recovery and social reintegration, which corresponds to resocialisation/rehabilitation and reintegration services.

3.10.rationale: The policy explicitly includes economic empowerment as part of recovery and social reintegration efforts, indicating economic support/empowerment services.

6.5.evidence:
Article 2
Letter a What is meant by "non-discrimination" is protection for all victims of gender-based violence and children without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race, class, gender, ethnic group, culture and language, legal status and physical or mental condition.
Letter b What is meant by "best interests of the victim" is that all actions concerning victims carried out by the government, community, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, the best interests of the victim must be the primary consideration.
Letter c What is meant by "gender justice" is fair treatment given to both women and men.
What is meant by "gender equality" is a condition and position that describes harmonious, appropriate and balanced relations between men and women in obtaining opportunities/chances in access, participation, control and benefits in the implementation of development as well as enjoying the results of development in family life as well as in society, nation and state.
Letter d What is meant by "victim protection" is providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
Letter e What is meant by "child survival" is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to identity.
What is meant by "child growth and development" is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to create and recreate.
Letter f What is meant by "respect for the child's opinion" is respect for children's rights to participate and express their opinions in decision-making which can be taken into consideration especially if it concerns matters that affect their lives.
Letter g What is meant by "openness" is that in the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children it is transparent among integrated service providers.
Letter h What is meant by "integration" is that in the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children it is carried out by building coordination among service providers, including medical services, legal advocates, psychologists, spiritual counselors, social workers, police.
Letter i What is meant by "empowering" is that every effort provided must be able to strengthen victims, both physically, psychologically, socially and economically.
Letter j What is meant by "victim confidentiality" is every action taken to ensure victims are in a safe condition from threats or other actions that threaten the life and psychology of victims.
